statement: The supplied source contains no derivation for the affine transformation of a Gaussian distribution; it only states the result as a property. If $\mathbf{Y} = \mathbf{c} + \mathbf{B}\mathbf{X}$ is an affine transformation of $\mathbf{X} \sim \mathcal{N}(\boldsymbol{\mu}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma})$, where $\mathbf{c}$ is an $M \times 1$ vector of constants and $\mathbf{B}$ is a constant $M \times N$ matrix, then $\mathbf{Y}$ has a multivariate normal distribution with expected value $\mathbf{c} + \mathbf{B}\boldsymbol{\mu}$ and variance $\mathbf{B}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\mathbf{B}^{\mathrm{T}}$, i.e., $\mathbf{Y} \sim \mathcal{N}\left(\mathbf{c} + \mathbf{B}\boldsymbol{\mu}, \mathbf{B}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\mathbf{B}^{\mathrm{T}}\right)$.

symbols.meaning: affine transformed random vector c + BX

properties.property: Normality preservation: $\mathbf{Y} = \mathbf{c} + \mathbf{B}\mathbf{X}$ has a multivariate normal distribution $\mathbf{Y} \sim \mathcal{N}\left(\mathbf{c} + \mathbf{B}\boldsymbol{\mu}, \mathbf{B}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\mathbf{B}^{\mathrm{T}}\right)$
properties.why: affine transformation of a multivariate normal vector preserves multivariate normality

properties.property: Expected value of the affine transformation is $\mathbb{E}[\mathbf{Y}] = \mathbf{c} + \mathbf{B}\boldsymbol{\mu}$
properties.why: linear transformation scales the mean vector by $\mathbf{B}$ and shifts it by constant $\mathbf{c}$

properties.property: Variance of the affine transformation is $\operatorname{Var}(\mathbf{Y}) = \mathbf{B}\boldsymbol{\Sigma}\mathbf{B}^{\mathrm{T}}$
properties.why: covariance matrix transforms via pre-multiplication by $\mathbf{B}$ and post-multiplication by $\mathbf{B}^{\mathrm{T}}$

properties.property: Univariate linear combination condition: a random vector is $k$-variate normally distributed if every linear combination of its $k$ components has a univariate normal distribution
properties.why: equivalent characterization defining the multivariate normal distribution

assumptions.assumption: X is distributed according to an N-dimensional multivariate normal distribution N(\mu, \Sigma)
assumptions.breaks_when: X is non-Gaussian or components do not jointly form a multivariate normal distribution

assumptions.assumption: B is an M x N matrix of constants
assumptions.breaks_when: B is stochastic or has number of columns not equal to N

assumptions.assumption: c is an M x 1 vector of constants
assumptions.breaks_when: c is stochastic or has dimension different from M x 1

failure_modes.signature: Matrix product BX or vector addition c + BX is undefined
failure_modes.cause: Number of columns of B does not match length N of X, or length of c does not match row dimension M of B

failure_modes.mode: Loss of Gaussianity from nonlinear or random transformation
failure_modes.signature: Transformed vector Y is not multivariate normal
failure_modes.cause: Transformation depends nonlinearly on X, or coefficients B and c are random variables

shape: expected a derivation, produced a definition
